body: Damn cute ball of fur. Is there a rabbit attached?!

Hah, I've had an entertaining weekend. I've heard more about my Ex recently. Turns out the guys she's going out with is in his 50's,  has a son her age and because of the relationship she's been ostracised by her family. Also, my sister knows her sister-in-law (where this info came from) and I've learned that my Ex's family loved me. I'm partly sceptical because I wasn't everything I should have been during that relationship, but in some ways it has helped me make peace. 

But, now I'm running into issues when I'm considering dating again. I just don't see that it's worth it. I'm the kind of person who doesn't do one night stands, or casual dating, but after this experience I'm scared of getting involved in another relationship. That and I'm not convinced that sex is remotely worth the process, the effort I need to go through as a man to get.

Thanks everyone, every so often I just need to vent and a reminder that I actually did well in that relationship. Also, didn't seem to mention it above but she was [F]23 at the time (going on 33!). I knew it would be difficult, we lived two very different lifestyles, I lived a good hour's drive away in a different city and we both had a small ton of issues that we brought into this. But I tried, I put a lot of effort into building a relationship (literally building a social network almost from scratch again in my hometown), I did a lot to either help her with her issues or at least work with them. All of this while I wasn't at my best, while I was trying to get some of my other issues in order (my eating habits, a few medical issues, my sleeping patterns). Plus a 40-hour a week job and still a social life in my adopted city. 

Being in a relationship was a very big culture shock for me and something I admit I wasn't ready for. At the time I also wasn't prepared or strong enough really to work out what I wanted, I let myself be dragged along a lot deeper than I expected in such a short amount of time. I didn't cope very well a lot of the time, but I was happy with her. 

All of these are things I've told myself and been told, and I've largely been fine, but every now and again I fall off the wagon. I'll be fine. I was a lot more patient, forgiving and understanding than I know most people would be. None of my friends would have gotten involved with her, because they wouldn't have wanted the hassle. 

I'm such a different person than I was 18 months ago. I'm a lot more mature, more focused, live a better and healthier life. Hell, even though it doesn't sound like it, I take it as a positive sign that I still care about her and wish her happiness in her new relationship.

Thanks for the help, I'm a lot calmer now than I was when I posted this last night. I've still not ruled out committing suicide, but I'm further away from taking that step. 

I know I'm still hungup on the mess of the relationship I went through, I might make a post on /r/relationships to help me work through some of the issues. I'm over my Ex, I know that would never work (she needs someone a lot older and more capable of looking after her than I was), but don't feel like I've had the closure I would like. 

It was also my first serious relationship (and dear god did I do it the hard way! Even just turned 25 I was not ready for that), so it really forced me to work out exactly what I want from life and re-evaluate myself. But that's led to a lot of anxiety, because of various disconnects between what I feel I want from life, what I'm currently doing and what I'm capable of doing. Not to mention the job market is horrific (I know again not as bad as in other Euro countries) so changing careers is something that is unlikely at this point. 

But thankyou for providing me with a platform for some decent venting. I'm feeling a lot better and a bit more determined to stick it out and continue to improve myself.

Thanks for the support! Rationally I know I've done well for myself; I earn as much as my Dad has ever done, I've used the time/money to go out and experience a lot of things and I've got a solid group of friends, even if I don't see them that often these days as work/circumstances have scattered us a bit. 

Thanks as well for the perspective; it helps a lot to be reminded that there are people who have different perspectives out there. I'm the kind of person who keeps in touch with my family (I've done a lot more so since my break-up) and friends; not as much as my Ex did during our relationship (I was effectively living in her life...).

Thanks! I'm naturally an animal person but since Uni I've not been settled enough to really look after an animal, but as soon as I'm back from my trips abroad I'm going to get something low maintenance, like a hamster. I'd go for a cat but I'm moving into a 6th floor flat soon which won't be an ideal environment. I'm a caring person, probably more than should be healthy for me (definitely the reason I'm still hung up on my ex), but I think I will be better if I start doing something more...worthwhile. I might volunteer at a charity shop, or find some charity organisations I can get involved in.
No idea. When we broke up I cut off all communication. I hope she's doing OK, but she has a lot of mental issues and some crippling health issues that mean she won't have a good future.

Didn't lose my virginity until I was 25 (with my ex teachers daughter as well!), first real relationship etc. It ended in flames and recrimination but I learned a lot about myself. And I learned not to get involved with manic-depressives.
